title: Three thousand deletions by one merge patch from a mapping of half a million keys must stay linear
notes: The input is a block mapping of 500,000 keys, `k000000: value` to `k499999: value`, 7.5 megabytes. One RFC 7396 merge patch deletes 3,000 of them with `"kN": null` members (section 2: a null member removes the key). The deleted keys come in thirty runs of a hundred, starting at `k001000`, `k017666`, `k034332` and so on, every 16,666 keys, so the deletions are spread over the whole mapping and a library cannot finish by touching one place. Every other line stays as it was, and a removed entry takes only its own line (there are no comments here, so no convention is involved). The result is the same 7.5 megabytes without those 3,000 lines, which is far larger than a stored file may be, so the exact bytes come from a recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md): the kept keys in thirty-one runs. The patch is valid and its result is small enough that no limit applies to it, so the exact result is the expected answer; a limit error is also accepted, because a library may bound the work or the output of a patch, and then the document must be reported unchanged (a patch is atomic). A library that finishes by rewriting or moving the rest of the document once per deleted key moves on average half of 7.5 megabytes 3,000 times, which is about 11 gigabytes of copying, and goes over the time bound. The time bound is derived from the siblings, not from a measurement of any library: safety/one-line-flow-mapping-ten-megabytes allows 10 seconds for about ten megabytes, about 1 second per megabyte, and safety/patch-many-appends-into-a-created-flow-sequence allows 2 seconds for a result under one megabyte, about 2 seconds per megabyte; for 7.5 megabytes that is 7.5 to 15 seconds, and the bound is the common 10 seconds (the runner stretches it by at most 8 on a slow machine, as for every bounded case). The memory bound is 2048 MB, as in the ten-megabyte sibling, whose accepted answer is also a structure of about a million nodes held in memory: this input has a million scalar nodes and the result is held as well. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The input and the expected result are generated from the recipes in case.json; the case carries the tag `slow` because both are larger than a stored file.

provenance.reference: A patch engine whose merge-patch deletions skipped its work bound, so three thousand deletions from a large mapping each moved the rest of the document and took quadratic time.
